courses.title: Big Data Fundamentals
courses.tagline: What 'big data' really means, how data is stored and spread across machines, and how the whole ecosystem fits together.

modules.title: Introduction
modules.summary: The big data problem and where it came from.

lessons.title: What is big data? The 5 Vs explained
lessons.description: What big data really means, explained with the 5 Vs: Volume, Velocity, Variety, Veracity and Value. Real Indian examples (UPI, canteen orders, food delivery), animations, Python programs you can run, a line-by-line tracer, quiz and interview scenarios.

lessons.title: Why one computer is not enough for big data
lessons.description: The storage, memory, CPU, I/O and reliability limits of a single computer, vertical vs horizontal scaling, and why big data needs clusters. Real calculations, animations, Python simulations you can run, a memory test for your own PC, quiz and interview scenarios.

lessons.title: Distributed computing basics for big data
lessons.description: How distributed computing works: partitioning, parallel processing, data locality, aggregation, master and workers, replication and fault tolerance. Exam-evaluation analogy, animations, Python simulations of a mini cluster, a multi-core program for your PC, quiz and interview scenarios.

lessons.title: A short history of big data: from one server to the lakehouse
lessons.description: The history of big data explained simply: the 1997 origin of the term, the 3 Vs, Google's GFS, MapReduce and Bigtable papers, Hadoop, Hive, NoSQL, Kafka, Spark, cloud warehouses, the lakehouse and AI. Five eras, the forces behind them, animations, Python programs, quiz and interview questions.

modules.title: Data and Storage
modules.summary: What big data looks like and where it lives.

lessons.title: Structured, semi-structured and unstructured data
lessons.description: Structured, semi-structured and unstructured data explained with a food-delivery order: schemas, JSON nesting and flattening, log parsing, metadata, turning text into labels, schema drift and data contracts. Beginner to Advanced, real-time animations, Python you can run in the browser and on your PC.

lessons.title: File formats for big data: CSV, JSON, Avro, Parquet and ORC
lessons.description: CSV vs JSON vs Avro vs Parquet vs ORC explained: row vs columnar storage, text vs binary, schemas, compression codecs (gzip, snappy, zstd), splittable files, dictionary and run-length encoding, row groups, predicate pushdown and Avro schema evolution with a Schema Registry. Real size comparison you can run on your PC.

lessons.title: Storage for big data: block, file and object storage (and HDFS)
lessons.description: Block vs file vs object storage explained for big data: buckets, keys and prefixes, HDFS blocks and replication, NameNode and DataNodes, durability, erasure coding, storage tiers and lifecycle rules, the small-files problem and why renames are unsafe on S3. Real-time animations, Python you can run, and a mini object store on your PC.

lessons.title: NoSQL databases: key-value, document, wide-column and graph
lessons.description: NoSQL databases explained: key-value (Redis, DynamoDB), document (MongoDB), wide-column (Cassandra, HBase) and graph (Neo4j), SQL vs NoSQL, query-first data modelling, partition keys, denormalisation, TTL, ACID vs BASE, tunable consistency and polyglot persistence. Real-time animations, Python simulations and a NoSQL lab on your PC.

modules.title: Distributed Systems Concepts
modules.summary: The ideas every big data tool is built on.

lessons.title: Scaling up vs scaling out (and back-of-envelope estimation)
lessons.description: Vertical vs horizontal scaling in depth: stateless vs stateful services, load balancers, autoscaling, read replicas, headroom, the Universal Scalability Law, Little's law and tail latency, plus a step-by-step back-of-envelope estimation method for requests, storage, bandwidth and servers. Diwali-night animations and a capacity estimator for your PC.

lessons.title: Partitioning and sharding: splitting data across machines
lessons.description: Partitioning and sharding explained: range, hash, directory and composite partitioning, choosing a partition key, routing and scatter-gather queries, rebalancing, consistent hashing with virtual nodes, hot keys and date hotspots, local vs global indexes, and partitions in HDFS, Spark, Kafka, Cassandra and data lakes. Real SQLite shards on your PC.

lessons.title: Replication: leaders, followers and copies
lessons.description: Replication explained: single-leader, multi-leader and leaderless replication, synchronous vs asynchronous vs semi-synchronous, replication lag and read-your-writes, failover, RPO and RTO, Kafka acks and in-sync replicas, quorums, split brain, fencing tokens and consensus (Raft). Real-time animations and a replication simulator for your PC.

lessons.title: The CAP theorem and consistency models
lessons.description: The CAP theorem explained correctly: consistency, availability and partition tolerance, CP vs AP systems, why “pick two” is a myth, PACELC, the consistency ladder (linearizable, sequential, causal, read-your-writes, eventual), tunable quorums, last-write-wins, version vectors and CRDTs. UPI vs Instagram-likes examples, animations and a partition simulator for your PC.

modules.title: The Ecosystem
modules.summary: The tools, the architectures and how they fit.

lessons.title: The big data ecosystem map: every tool in its place
lessons.description: Make sense of Hadoop, Spark, Kafka, Hive, Airflow and 40 more tools by sorting them into six layers: ingest, store, process, query, visualise and orchestrate. Real-time scenarios (lunch rush, a 2 am failure, moving to the cloud), Beginner to Advanced explanations, Python simulations, quiz and interview scenarios.

lessons.title: Batch vs stream processing: now or later?
lessons.description: Batch vs stream processing explained with live cricket scores, UPI fraud checks and food-delivery orders: latency, throughput, tumbling, sliding and session windows, event time, watermarks, late data and delivery guarantees. Beginner to Advanced, real-time animations, Python simulations and a live stream you can run on your PC.

lessons.title: Data lake vs data warehouse (and the lakehouse)
lessons.description: Data lake vs data warehouse vs lakehouse: schema-on-read vs schema-on-write, ETL vs ELT, bronze/silver/gold zones, star schema, Parquet, partitioning and the data swamp. Beginner to Advanced, real-time animations, Python simulations and a mini lake + SQL warehouse you build on your PC.

lessons.title: Lambda and Kappa architectures explained
lessons.description: Lambda architecture (batch, speed and serving layers) and Kappa architecture (one stream path with log replay) explained with a Diwali sale dashboard: why live and final numbers differ, how views are merged, how to replay Kafka after a bug, and how to choose. Beginner to Advanced, real-time animations, Python simulations and a replay demo for your PC.

lessons.title: Data pipelines and orchestration (Apache Airflow basics)
lessons.description: Data pipelines and orchestration explained: DAGs, tasks, operators and sensors, scheduling with cron, dependencies, retries and alerts, logical dates and data intervals, backfills, idempotent tasks, incremental loads, late data and quality gates, with Apache Airflow examples and a mini orchestrator you run on your PC.

lessons.title: Big data on the cloud: AWS, Azure and GCP
lessons.description: Big data on the cloud explained: IaaS, managed services and serverless, the equivalent big data services on AWS, Azure and Google Cloud (S3, EMR, Glue, Athena, Redshift, Databricks, Synapse/Fabric, BigQuery, Dataproc, Dataflow, Kinesis, Event Hubs, Pub/Sub), India regions, cost meters and FinOps, spot instances, egress, lock-in, security and RBI data residency. Animations and a cloud bill estimator for your PC.

lessons.title: Big data at Indian scale: UPI, IRCTC, live cricket and sale days
lessons.description: Case studies of big data at Indian scale: UPI payments (24 billion a month), IRCTC Tatkal rush (37,410 tickets a minute), live cricket streaming (5.9 crore concurrent viewers) and e-commerce sale days. Learn to convert headline numbers into TPS and peaks, and the techniques behind them: waiting rooms, rate limiting, idempotency, caching, CDNs, partitioning and streaming analytics. Animations and a load estimator for your PC.

lessons.title: Data quality, governance, security and the DPDP Act
lessons.description: Data quality dimensions (accuracy, completeness, consistency, timeliness, validity, uniqueness), quality checks and quarantine in pipelines, data governance (ownership, catalogs, lineage, classification, data contracts), security (RBAC, masking, row filters, encryption, audit logs) and privacy under India's Digital Personal Data Protection Act 2023 and DPDP Rules 2025: consent, erasure, breach notification and penalties. Animations and a data-quality gate for your PC.

lessons.title: Data engineer vs data analyst vs data scientist
lessons.description: Data engineer, data analyst and data scientist compared: what each does, skills and tools, a day in the life, career paths, adjacent roles (analytics engineer, ML engineer), indicative 2026 salary ranges in India, and how to choose. Beginner to Advanced, real-time scenarios, Python tools to test your fit, quiz and interview questions.

lessons.title: Data engineering roadmap, portfolio, certifications and resume
lessons.description: A practical data engineering career plan for India: a skills roadmap from SQL and Python to Spark, Airflow, Kafka, cloud and lakehouse, portfolio project ideas with Indian data, how to build a GitHub repository reviewers trust, which certifications to choose (AWS DEA-C01, Microsoft DP-700, Google Professional Data Engineer, Databricks, Snowflake, Confluent), and how to write a one-page resume with quantified bullets. Animations and a roadmap planner and resume-bullet scorer for your PC.

lessons.title: Big data and data engineering interview questions with answers
lessons.description: The most common data engineering interview questions with model answers: SQL (joins, window functions, deduplication, second highest), Python, big data concepts (5 Vs, ETL vs ELT, lake vs warehouse vs lakehouse, Parquet, partitioning, CAP), Spark (shuffles, skew, broadcast joins, repartition vs coalesce), Kafka and streaming, data modelling (star schema, SCD type 2), pipeline design and behavioural questions. Animations, a scoring rubric and SQL practice for your PC.

lessons.title: Capstone: build a mini data pipeline on your PC
lessons.description: Capstone project for Big Data Fundamentals: build an end-to-end medallion pipeline on your own computer with Python and Parquet. Raw JSON lines to bronze Parquet partitioned by date, silver with deduplication, a data quality gate, quarantine and masked PII, gold business tables and a report, with idempotent re-runs. Includes row reconciliation, an append-vs-overwrite experiment, a map to Spark, Delta Lake and Airflow, extensions and a README template.

lessons.title: Final test, cheat sheet and exam questions: Big Data Fundamentals
lessons.description: Revise all of Big Data Fundamentals: a one-page course map, cheat sheets of numbers and comparisons (scale up vs out, row vs columnar, lake vs warehouse, batch vs streaming, MapReduce vs Spark, CP vs AP, ETL vs ELT), how to write 2-, 5- and 10-mark answers, estimation practice, 2-mark and 5-mark questions with model answers, a 50-mark practice paper generator for your PC and a 25-question final test.

courses.title: Core Java
courses.tagline: From your first println to threads and streams, see what the JVM does at every step.

modules.title: Introduction to Java
modules.summary: What Java is, why it runs everywhere, and what happens when you press Run.

lessons.title: What is Java and why learn it?
lessons.description: What is Java? Definition, history, editions, how Java runs on any device (write once, run anywhere), real-world uses, runnable code, a line-by-line JVM tracer and a quiz.

lessons.title: History and key features of Java
lessons.description: History of Java from Oak (1991) to Java 25, and the key features of Java (simple, object-oriented, platform independent, robust, secure, multithreaded and more) explained with animations, runnable code, a JVM tracer and a quiz.

lessons.title: JDK vs JRE vs JVM
lessons.description: JDK vs JRE vs JVM explained: what each one contains, how they fit inside each other, the JVM's parts (class loader, memory areas, execution engine), with animations, runnable code, a JVM tracer, quiz and industry interview scenarios.

lessons.title: How Java code runs: source → bytecode → JVM
lessons.description: How a Java program runs step by step: javac compile phases, the .class file and bytecode (javap), class loading, linking and initialization, the interpreter and the JIT compiler. With animations, runnable code, a bytecode tracer, quiz and industry interview scenarios.

lessons.title: Installing Java and your first program
lessons.description: Install the JDK on Windows, macOS or Linux, set JAVA_HOME and PATH, choose an editor, and write, compile and run your first Java program. Includes the most common beginner errors and how to fix them, animations, runnable code, a tracer, quiz and industry scenarios.

lessons.title: Structure of a Java program (class, main, statements)
lessons.description: The structure of a Java program: package, imports, class, fields, methods, the main method word by word, statements, blocks and comments, and what System.out.println really is. With animations, runnable code, a stack tracer, quiz and industry interview scenarios.

modules.title: Language Basics
modules.summary: Variables, data types, operators and taking input from the user.

lessons.title: Variables: boxes in memory
lessons.description: Java variables explained: declaration, initialisation and assignment, naming rules, final constants, var, scope, and local vs instance vs static variables, with where each one lives in memory. Animations, runnable code, a stack tracer, quiz and industry scenarios.

lessons.title: Primitive data types (int, double, char, boolean…)
lessons.description: Java's 8 primitive data types explained: byte, short, int, long, float, double, char and boolean, with sizes, ranges, literals, integer overflow and floating-point surprises shown bit by bit. Animations, runnable code, a tracer, quiz and industry scenarios.

lessons.title: Reference types and how they differ
lessons.description: Java reference types explained: objects on the heap, references as arrows, aliasing, null and NullPointerException, == vs equals, and how references differ from primitives. With animations, runnable code, a heap tracer, quiz and industry scenarios.

lessons.title: Type casting: widening and narrowing
lessons.description: Java type casting explained: automatic widening conversions, explicit narrowing casts, data loss and truncation, numeric promotion in expressions, compound assignment, and casting vs parsing. With bit-level animations, runnable code, a tracer, quiz and industry scenarios.

lessons.title: Operators: arithmetic, relational, logical, bitwise
lessons.description: Java operators explained: arithmetic and remainder, increment and decrement, assignment, relational, logical with short-circuiting, bitwise and shift operators, the ternary operator, precedence and associativity. Animations, runnable code, a tracer, quiz and industry scenarios.

lessons.title: Taking input with Scanner
lessons.description: Read keyboard input in Java with Scanner: nextInt, nextDouble, next and nextLine, the nextInt-then-nextLine trap, input validation with hasNextInt, InputMismatchException, closing Scanner, and BufferedReader for speed. Animations, runnable code, a tracer, quiz and industry scenarios.

lessons.title: Comments, keywords and naming conventions
lessons.description: Java comments (single-line, multi-line, Javadoc with @param and @return), reserved and contextual keywords, identifier rules, and the naming conventions used in industry: PascalCase, camelCase, UPPER_SNAKE_CASE and package names. Animations, runnable code, a tracer, quiz and industry scenarios.

modules.title: Control Flow
modules.summary: Making decisions and repeating work: if, switch and loops.

lessons.title: if, else-if and else
lessons.description: Java if, if-else, else-if ladders and nested if explained with a grading example: conditions, braces, the dangling else, order of checks, guard clauses, and the bytecode jumps behind every if. Animations, runnable code, a tracer, quiz and industry scenarios.

lessons.title: switch statement and switch expressions
lessons.description: Java switch explained: classic switch with case, break, default and fall-through; switch on int, char, String and enum; modern switch expressions with arrows, multiple labels and yield; exhaustiveness; and the tableswitch and lookupswitch bytecode behind it. Animations, runnable code, a tracer, quiz and industry scenarios.

lessons.title: for loop
lessons.description: The Java for loop explained: initialisation, condition and update, the exact order of execution, counting up, down and in steps, the enhanced for-each loop, loop variable scope, off-by-one errors and the bytecode back-jump. With animations, runnable code, a tracer, 10 practice problems, quiz and industry scenarios.

lessons.title: while and do-while loops
lessons.description: Java while and do-while loops explained: entry- vs exit-controlled loops, loops with an unknown number of iterations, sentinel values, digit-by-digit number processing, infinite loops and how to end them, and the bytecode difference. With animations, runnable code, a tracer, 10 practice problems, quiz and industry scenarios.

lessons.title: break, continue and labelled loops
lessons.description: Java break and continue explained: leaving a loop early, skipping an iteration, labelled break and continue for nested loops, break inside switch, return vs break, and the goto jumps behind them. With animations, runnable code, a tracer, 8 practice problems, quiz and industry scenarios.

lessons.title: Nested loops and pattern printing
lessons.description: Java nested loops explained: how the inner loop runs completely for each outer iteration, counting iterations, the row-and-column method for star and number patterns, grids and tables, and why nested loops get slow on big data. With animations, a tracer, 13 practice problems (patterns and business tasks), quiz and industry scenarios.

modules.title: Arrays and Strings
modules.summary: Storing many values together and working with text.

lessons.title: One-dimensional arrays
lessons.description: Java one-dimensional arrays explained: declaring and creating arrays, indexes from 0, length, default values, looping with for and for-each, ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException, reference copies vs real copies, and the Arrays helper class. With animations, a tracer, 12 practice problems (including business tasks), quiz and industry scenarios.

lessons.title: Two-dimensional arrays
lessons.description: Java two-dimensional arrays explained: an array of arrays, creating rectangular and jagged arrays, [row][col] indexing, length of rows and columns, nested-loop traversal, deepToString, and shallow vs deep copies. With animations, a tracer, 11 practice problems (matrices and business tasks), quiz and industry scenarios.

lessons.title: String class and immutability
lessons.description: Java String class explained: what a String object is, ways to create Strings, length() and charAt(), concatenation rules, and immutability: why methods like toUpperCase() return new Strings, what reassignment really does, and why Java designed String this way. With animations, a tracer, 11 practice problems (including business tasks), quiz and industry scenarios.

lessons.title: String pool: == vs equals()
lessons.description: Java String pool explained: how string literals are shared, why new String() creates a separate object, the difference between == (same object) and equals() (same characters), compile-time constants, intern(), equalsIgnoreCase, compareTo and null-safe comparison. With animations, a tracer, 9 practice problems (including business tasks), quiz and industry scenarios.

lessons.title: Common String methods
lessons.description: The Java String methods you'll use every day: trim and strip, toUpperCase and toLowerCase, indexOf and lastIndexOf, contains, startsWith, endsWith, substring (end index excluded), split (it takes a regex!), replace vs replaceAll, join, repeat, format, isEmpty vs isBlank, and parsing numbers. With animations, a tracer, 13 practice problems (including business tasks), quiz and industry scenarios.

lessons.title: StringBuilder and StringBuffer
lessons.description: Java StringBuilder and StringBuffer explained: mutable strings, append, insert, delete, replace, reverse and setCharAt, length vs capacity and how the buffer grows, why building text in a loop with + is slow, toString, the equals() trap, and when to use StringBuffer for thread safety. With animations, a tracer, 11 practice problems (including business tasks), quiz and industry scenarios.

modules.title: Methods
modules.summary: Breaking programs into reusable pieces, and what the call stack does.

lessons.title: Defining and calling methods
lessons.description: Java methods explained from zero: why methods (reuse and readability), the method header (modifiers, return type, name, parameters), static methods called from main, void vs returning methods, and the call stack with frames pushed and popped. With animations, a tracer, 11 practice problems (including business tasks), quiz and industry scenarios.

lessons.title: Parameters and return values
lessons.description: Java method parameters and return values explained: parameters vs arguments, matching by order and type, return types, early return and guard clauses, returning arrays, and the compile errors missing return statement, unreachable statement and incompatible types. With animations, a tracer, 12 practice problems (including business tasks), quiz and industry scenarios.

lessons.title: Pass-by-value in Java
lessons.description: Java is always pass-by-value, explained visually: primitive arguments are copied, object arguments copy the reference, so mutating an object is visible but reassigning a parameter is not. The failed swap, arrays, Strings and StringBuilder as parameters. With animations, a tracer, 11 practice problems (including business tasks), quiz and industry scenarios.

lessons.title: Method overloading
lessons.description: Method overloading in Java: same method name, different parameter lists. Learn the rules (number, type and order of parameters), why the return type alone is not enough, how javac picks a method (exact match, widening, boxing, varargs), ambiguous calls, and real uses like println. With animations, a JVM tracer, 8 practice problems, quiz and interview scenarios.

lessons.title: Recursion and the call stack
lessons.description: Recursion in Java explained with the call stack: base case and recursive case, how each call gets its own frame, how values return back up, StackOverflowError, recursion vs loops, and classic examples (factorial, sum of digits, power, binary search, folder sizes). With animations, a JVM tracer, 8 practice problems, quiz and interview scenarios.

lessons.title: Variable arguments (varargs)
lessons.description: Varargs in Java: methods that accept any number of arguments with type... name. Learn the rules (one varargs parameter, always last), how javac packs the arguments into an array, calling with zero arguments, passing an array directly, varargs and overloading, and real uses like String.format, printf and List.of. With animations, a JVM tracer, 8 practice problems, quiz and interview scenarios.

modules.title: Object-Oriented Programming: Basics
modules.summary: Classes, objects, constructors and the keywords that hold them together.

lessons.title: Classes and objects
lessons.description: Java classes and objects explained: a class as a blueprint, fields and methods, creating objects with new, reference variables, default field values, many objects from one class, two references to one object, null and NullPointerException. With animations, a tracer, 10 practice problems (including business tasks), quiz and industry scenarios.

lessons.title: Constructors and constructor chaining
lessons.description: Java constructors explained: the default constructor and when it disappears, no-arg and parameterized constructors, constructor overloading, chaining with this(...), why there is no return type, and the exact initialization order of fields, instance blocks and constructor bodies. With animations, a tracer, 10 practice problems (including business tasks), quiz and industry scenarios.

lessons.title: The this keyword
lessons.description: Java this keyword explained: the hidden reference to the current object, fixing field vs parameter shadowing with this.field, calling constructors with this(...), passing this to other objects, returning this for fluent method chains, and why this can't be used in static code. With animations, a tracer, 10 practice problems (including business tasks), quiz and industry scenarios.

lessons.title: The static keyword
lessons.description: The static keyword in Java: static variables shared by all objects, static methods called without an object, static blocks that run once when a class loads, static imports, and the 'non-static variable cannot be referenced from a static context' error. With animations, a JVM tracer that shows static fields, 8 practice problems, quiz and interview scenarios.

lessons.title: Access modifiers
lessons.description: Access modifiers in Java: public, protected, default (package-private) and private. Who can see a class, field, method or constructor, the access table every exam asks for, one field tried with all four modifiers (what compiles and what prints), the 'has private access' compile error, the protected rule across packages, private constructors, and how access control protects real systems. With animations, a JVM tracer, 8 practice problems, quiz and interview scenarios.

lessons.title: Packages and imports
lessons.description: Packages and imports in Java: the package statement, folder structure, fully qualified names, single-type and wildcard imports, java.lang, static imports, name clashes like java.util.Date vs java.sql.Date, compiling with javac -d and running with java -cp. With animations, a JVM tracer, 8 practice problems, quiz and interview scenarios.

modules.title: Object-Oriented Programming: The Four Pillars
modules.summary: Encapsulation, inheritance, polymorphism and abstraction with real-world models.

lessons.title: Encapsulation: getters and setters
lessons.description: Java encapsulation explained: private fields, getters and setters with validation, read-only properties, why public fields break a bank balance, immutable classes and defensive copies. With animations, a tracer, JVM-traced worked examples, 10 practice problems (including business tasks), quiz and industry scenarios.

lessons.title: Inheritance and types of inheritance
lessons.description: Java inheritance explained: extends and the IS-A relationship, single, multilevel and hierarchical inheritance, why Java has no multiple inheritance of classes (the diamond problem) and how interfaces help, what is and isn't inherited, and Object at the root. With animations, a tracer, JVM-traced worked examples, 10 practice problems, quiz and industry scenarios.

lessons.title: The super keyword
lessons.description: Java super keyword explained: super(...) to call a parent constructor and why it must be the first statement, the implicit super() javac inserts, the compile error when the parent has no no-argument constructor, super.method(), field hiding with super.field, and the parent-to-child order of constructor execution. With animations, a tracer, JVM-traced worked examples, 10 practice problems, quiz and industry scenarios.

lessons.title: Method overriding
lessons.description: Java method overriding explained: same signature in the child class, the @Override annotation and the mistakes it catches, the rules (access can't be narrower, covariant return types, checked exceptions can't widen), why static, private and final methods can't be overridden, static method hiding, and a first look at dynamic dispatch. With animations, a tracer, JVM-traced worked examples, 10 practice problems, quiz and industry scenarios.

lessons.title: Polymorphism: compile-time and runtime
lessons.description: Java polymorphism explained: compile-time polymorphism with method overloading, runtime polymorphism with overriding, upcasting, dynamic method dispatch decided by the object's runtime class, downcasting with instanceof, pattern matching for instanceof (Java 16) and ClassCastException. With animations, a tracer, JVM-traced worked examples, 10 practice problems, quiz and industry scenarios.

lessons.title: Abstraction with abstract classes
lessons.description: Java abstraction with abstract classes explained: abstract methods and classes, why an abstract class can't be instantiated (with the real compiler error), constructors in abstract classes, partial implementation shared by subclasses, and the template method pattern. With animations, a tracer, JVM-traced worked examples, 10 practice problems, quiz and industry scenarios.

lessons.title: Interfaces (default and static methods)
lessons.description: Java interfaces explained: interfaces as contracts, implementing multiple interfaces, constants, default methods (Java 8) and the diamond rule with X.super.m(), static methods, private methods (Java 9), interface vs abstract class, and a first look at functional interfaces. With animations, a tracer, JVM-traced worked examples, 10 practice problems, quiz and industry scenarios.

lessons.title: The final keyword
lessons.description: Java final keyword explained: final local variables and fields, blank finals that must be assigned exactly once, effectively final variables, final parameters, final methods, final classes like String, and why a final reference does not make an object immutable. With animations, a tracer, JVM-traced worked examples, 10 practice problems, quiz and industry scenarios.

modules.title: Inside the JVM: Memory
modules.summary: Stack, heap, garbage collection and class loading, the behind-the-scenes view.

lessons.title: Stack vs heap memory
lessons.description: Java stack vs heap explained: per-thread stacks of frames (locals, operand stack, return info), the shared heap for objects and arrays, references pointing from stack to heap, metaspace for class data, -Xss and -Xmx, and real StackOverflowError and OutOfMemoryError messages. With animations, a JVM tracer, 9 practice problems, quiz and industry scenarios.

lessons.title: Object lifecycle
lessons.description: The Java object lifecycle explained: allocation, zero-filled defaults and the constructor chain, use, becoming unreachable by reassignment, null or scope end, reachability from GC roots, islands of isolation, why finalize() is deprecated, and Cleaner and try-with-resources instead. With animations, a JVM tracer, 8 practice problems, quiz and industry scenarios.

lessons.title: Garbage collection
lessons.description: Java garbage collection explained: the generational idea (Eden, survivor spaces, old generation), minor vs major and full GC, mark-sweep-compact, G1 as the default since Java 9, ZGC and Shenandoah, stop-the-world pauses, why System.gc() is only a request, memory leaks from static collections, unclosed resources and listeners, and how to read -Xlog:gc output. With animations, a JVM tracer, 8 practice problems, quiz and industry scenarios.

lessons.title: Class loaders and class loading
lessons.description: Java class loading explained: loading, linking (verify, prepare, resolve) and initialization, exactly when a class is initialized (first active use) with static block print-order demos, the bootstrap, platform and application class loaders, parent delegation, ClassNotFoundException vs NoClassDefFoundError, and -verbose:class. With animations, a JVM tracer, 8 practice problems, quiz and industry scenarios.

lessons.title: JIT compiler and performance
lessons.description: The Java JIT compiler explained: the interpreter runs first, hot code is detected with counters, tiered compilation moves methods from C1 to C2, inlining, escape analysis and dead code elimination at a high level, warm-up, deoptimisation, why naive timing benchmarks lie (and JMH), and how to read -XX:+PrintCompilation output. With animations, a JVM tracer, 7 practice problems, quiz and industry scenarios.

modules.title: Exception Handling
modules.summary: What happens when things go wrong, and how to recover gracefully.

lessons.title: What are exceptions? Exception hierarchy
lessons.description: Java exceptions explained: what happens when an exception is thrown, how the JVM searches the call stack for a handler, how to read a real stack trace, the Throwable, Error, Exception and RuntimeException hierarchy, and common exceptions with their real messages. With animations, a tracer, 11 practice problems, quiz and industry scenarios.

lessons.title: try, catch and finally
lessons.description: Java try, catch and finally explained: how control jumps from try to catch, multiple catch blocks and why the order matters, multi-catch (Java 7), why finally always runs (and the two cases when it doesn't), and the return-in-finally pitfall. With animations, a tracer, 11 practice problems including business tasks, quiz and industry scenarios.

lessons.title: Checked vs unchecked exceptions
lessons.description: Checked vs unchecked exceptions in Java: the catch-or-declare rule the compiler enforces, the 'unreported exception' compile error, examples of each kind, when to use which, and wrapping a checked exception in an unchecked one with its cause. With animations, a tracer, 11 practice problems, quiz and industry scenarios.

lessons.title: throw and throws
lessons.description: Java throw and throws explained: throwing your own exceptions to validate input, declaring checked exceptions with throws, how an exception propagates through several method frames, rethrowing, exception chaining with getCause(), and the overriding rules for throws. With animations, a tracer, 11 practice problems, quiz and industry scenarios.

lessons.title: Custom exceptions
lessons.description: Java custom exceptions explained: extending Exception vs RuntimeException, writing the message and cause constructors, adding fields like a shortfall amount, business exceptions such as InsufficientFundsException, exception families, naming rules and when not to create one. With animations, a tracer, 11 practice problems, quiz and industry scenarios.

lessons.title: try-with-resources
lessons.description: Java try-with-resources explained: the AutoCloseable interface, resources closed automatically in reverse order, closing before catch and finally, suppressed exceptions and getSuppressed(), why it beats a manual finally, and Java 9 effectively-final resource variables. With animations, a tracer, 11 practice problems, quiz and industry scenarios.

modules.title: Core Classes and Language Features
modules.summary: Wrapper classes, the Object class, enums and inner classes.

lessons.title: Wrapper classes
lessons.description: Wrapper classes in Java: Integer, Double, Character, Boolean and the other four. Why primitives need object versions, valueOf vs parseInt, converting Strings to numbers, MAX_VALUE and MIN_VALUE, Character helper methods, the Integer cache (-128 to 127) and why == fails for 128. With animations, a JVM tracer, 8 practice problems, quiz and interview scenarios.

lessons.title: Autoboxing and unboxing
lessons.description: Autoboxing and unboxing in Java: how the compiler converts int to Integer and back for you, what javac really writes (valueOf and intValue, checked with javap), the NullPointerException when unboxing null, == between wrappers, list.remove(int) vs remove(Object), overloading rules, and the cost of boxing in loops. With animations, a JVM tracer, 8 practice problems, quiz and interview scenarios.

lessons.title: Object class: equals(), hashCode(), toString()
lessons.description: The Object class in Java: the root of every class and its 11 methods. How to override toString(), equals() and hashCode() correctly, the equals-hashCode contract, why a HashSet keeps duplicates when hashCode is missing, == vs equals, getClass vs instanceof, and Objects.equals / Objects.hash. With animations, a JVM tracer, 8 practice problems, quiz and interview scenarios.

lessons.title: Enums
lessons.description: Enums in Java: a fixed set of named constants that are real objects. values(), valueOf(), name() and ordinal(), switch on enums (classic and arrow form), enums with fields, constructors and methods, constant-specific behaviour, EnumMap and EnumSet, and what javac actually generates (checked with javap). With animations, a JVM tracer, 8 practice problems, quiz and interview scenarios.

lessons.title: Inner, static nested and anonymous classes
lessons.description: Nested classes in Java: inner (member) classes, static nested classes, local classes and anonymous classes. How to create each, what they can access, the hidden this$0 link to the outer object, Outer.this, effectively final captured variables, the .class files javac produces, and when to use which. With animations, a JVM tracer, 8 practice problems, quiz and interview scenarios.

modules.title: Collections Framework
modules.summary: Lists, sets and maps, plus how HashMap works internally.

lessons.title: Collections Framework overview
lessons.description: The Java Collections Framework: why arrays aren't enough, the interface hierarchy (Iterable, Collection, List, Set, Queue, Deque, Map), the main classes (ArrayList, LinkedList, HashSet, TreeSet, ArrayDeque, PriorityQueue, HashMap, TreeMap), how to choose one, immutable collections, and the Collections utility class. With animations, a JVM tracer, 8 practice problems, quiz and interview scenarios.

lessons.title: Generics
lessons.description: Generics in Java: type parameters for classes, interfaces and methods, why they replace casts and catch errors at compile time, the diamond operator, bounded types (T extends Comparable<T>), wildcards (? extends, ? super, PECS), type erasure proved with javap, raw types and the rules generics can't break. With animations, a JVM tracer, 8 practice problems, quiz and interview scenarios.

lessons.title: ArrayList
lessons.description: ArrayList in Java: a resizable array. Create, add, get, set, remove, search and sort; how it works inside (elementData, size vs capacity, default capacity 10, growth by 1.5x), the cost of each operation, remove(int) vs remove(Object), ConcurrentModificationException and removeIf, and when to choose something else. With animations, a JVM tracer, 8 practice problems, quiz and interview scenarios.

lessons.title: LinkedList
lessons.description: LinkedList in Java: a doubly linked list of nodes that implements both List and Deque. How nodes, first and last work, why adding and removing at the ends is O(1) but get(i) is O(n), LinkedList vs ArrayList vs ArrayDeque, using it as a queue and a stack, and when it's actually the right choice. With animations, a JVM tracer, 8 practice problems, quiz and interview scenarios.

lessons.title: HashSet, LinkedHashSet and TreeSet
lessons.description: Sets in Java: HashSet (fast, unordered), LinkedHashSet (insertion order) and TreeSet (sorted). How each one detects duplicates (hashCode/equals vs compareTo), what's inside (a HashMap, a linked hash map, a red-black tree), costs, TreeSet navigation methods (first, floor, ceiling, headSet), set operations (union, intersection, difference) and common traps. With animations, a JVM tracer, 8 practice problems, quiz and interview scenarios.

lessons.title: HashMap and how it works internally
lessons.description: HashMap in Java, inside and out: put, get, getOrDefault, merge and iterating entries; then the internals every interview asks about: the bucket table, hash() spreading, index = (n-1) & hash, collisions and chains, load factor 0.75 and resizing from 16 to 32 buckets, treeification at 8, null keys, mutable-key bugs, LinkedHashMap and TreeMap. Traced on the real JVM, with animations, 8 practice problems, quiz and interview scenarios.

lessons.title: Iterator and ListIterator
lessons.description: Iterator and ListIterator in Java: hasNext, next and remove; how the for-each loop uses an iterator; removing safely while looping; fail-fast iterators and ConcurrentModificationException (modCount); ListIterator's cursor, previous, set and add; fail-safe iterators of concurrent collections; and making your own class Iterable. With animations, a JVM tracer, 8 practice problems, quiz and interview scenarios.

lessons.title: Comparable vs Comparator
lessons.description: Sorting objects in Java: Comparable (compareTo, the natural order inside the class) vs Comparator (compare, any number of orders outside it). How sort calls your method, what negative/zero/positive mean, Comparator.comparing, thenComparing, reversed and nullsFirst, the subtraction overflow bug, consistency with equals, and sorting in TreeSet, TreeMap and PriorityQueue. With animations, a JVM tracer, 8 practice problems, quiz and interview scenarios.

modules.title: Multithreading
modules.summary: Running many tasks at once, and keeping them from clashing.

lessons.title: Processes vs threads
lessons.description: Processes vs threads in Java: what a process is, what a thread is, why threads share the heap but each has its own stack, the main thread, concurrency vs parallelism, cores, daemon threads and when the JVM exits. With animations, a JVM tracer, 8 practice problems, quiz and interview scenarios.

lessons.title: Creating threads: Thread vs Runnable
lessons.description: How to create threads in Java: extending Thread, implementing Runnable, lambdas and method references, thread names, start() vs run(), and why Runnable is preferred. With animations, a JVM tracer, 9 practice problems, quiz and interview scenarios.

lessons.title: Thread lifecycle
lessons.description: The Java thread lifecycle: the six Thread.State values NEW, RUNNABLE, BLOCKED, WAITING, TIMED_WAITING and TERMINATED, with sleep(), join(), join(timeout), interrupt(), isAlive() and getState(). With animations, a JVM tracer, 9 practice problems, quiz and interview scenarios.

lessons.title: Synchronization and race conditions
lessons.description: Race conditions and synchronization in Java: why count++ loses updates, critical sections, synchronized methods and blocks, monitor locks, static synchronized, volatile, AtomicInteger and deadlock. With animations, a JVM tracer, 9 practice problems, quiz and interview scenarios.

lessons.title: Inter-thread communication: wait() and notify()
lessons.description: Inter-thread communication in Java: wait(), notify() and notifyAll(), the monitor's wait set, why wait must be in a while loop, IllegalMonitorStateException, the producer-consumer pattern, BlockingQueue and CountDownLatch. With animations, a JVM tracer, 9 practice problems, quiz and interview scenarios.

lessons.title: ExecutorService and thread pools
lessons.description: ExecutorService and thread pools in Java: Executors factory methods, submit(), Callable vs Runnable, Future.get() with timeouts, invokeAll, shutdown() and awaitTermination(), RejectedExecutionException, CompletableFuture and Java 21 virtual threads. With animations, a JVM tracer, 9 practice problems, quiz and interview scenarios.

modules.title: File Handling and I/O
modules.summary: Reading and writing files, and saving objects to disk.

lessons.title: I/O streams: byte and character
lessons.description: Java I/O streams explained: byte streams (InputStream, OutputStream) vs character streams (Reader, Writer), read() returning -1, UTF-8 and charsets, InputStreamReader and OutputStreamWriter bridges, System.in/out/err and try-with-resources. With animations, a JVM tracer, 9 practice problems, quiz and interview scenarios.

lessons.title: Reading and writing files
lessons.description: Reading and writing files in Java: Path and Files (writeString, readString, readAllLines, write, APPEND, createDirectories, copy, move, delete), relative paths and the working directory, java.io.File, Scanner and PrintWriter, NoSuchFileException. With animations, a JVM tracer, 9 practice problems, quiz and interview scenarios.

lessons.title: BufferedReader and BufferedWriter
lessons.description: Buffered I/O in Java: why buffering is fast (fewer system calls), BufferedReader.readLine(), BufferedWriter.newLine(), flush() vs close(), the decorator pattern, BufferedInputStream/BufferedOutputStream and Files.newBufferedReader/Writer, plus processing large files line by line. With animations, a JVM tracer, 9 practice problems, quiz and interview scenarios.

lessons.title: Serialization and deserialization
lessons.description: Java serialization and deserialization: Serializable, ObjectOutputStream.writeObject, ObjectInputStream.readObject, transient and static fields, object graphs and shared references, serialVersionUID and InvalidClassException, NotSerializableException, constructors not running, and security risks with untrusted data. With animations, a JVM tracer, 9 practice problems, quiz and interview scenarios.

modules.title: Modern Java (Java 8 and later)
modules.summary: Lambdas, streams and the newer features used in today's projects.

lessons.title: Lambda expressions
lessons.description: Lambda expressions in Java: syntax forms, from anonymous classes to lambdas, type inference, effectively final captured variables, this inside a lambda, how invokedynamic runs lambdas, and using lambdas with sort, removeIf, replaceAll and forEach. With animations, a JVM tracer, 9 practice problems, quiz and interview scenarios.

lessons.title: Functional interfaces
lessons.description: Functional interfaces in Java: the single-abstract-method rule, @FunctionalInterface, java.util.function (Predicate, Function, Consumer, Supplier, BiFunction, UnaryOperator, BinaryOperator, primitive versions), default methods and/or/negate/andThen/compose, and the four kinds of method references. With animations, a JVM tracer, 9 practice problems, quiz and interview scenarios.

lessons.title: Stream API: filter, map, reduce
lessons.description: The Java Stream API: creating streams, intermediate operations (filter, map, sorted, distinct, limit) and terminal operations (collect, reduce, count, forEach, findFirst, anyMatch), lazy evaluation and one-element-at-a-time processing, IntStream, Collectors.groupingBy, counting, summingInt and joining, and single-use streams. With animations, a JVM tracer, 9 practice problems, quiz and interview scenarios.

lessons.title: Optional
lessons.description: Java Optional explained: why null causes NullPointerException, Optional.of, ofNullable and empty, orElse vs orElseGet, orElseThrow, ifPresent, map, filter and flatMap, Optional from streams, and where not to use Optional. With animations, a JVM tracer, 9 practice problems, quiz and interview scenarios.

lessons.title: var, records and text blocks
lessons.description: Modern Java features that cut boilerplate: local variable type inference with var (Java 10), records with generated constructors, accessors, equals, hashCode and toString, compact constructors for validation (Java 16), and text blocks for multi-line strings with formatted() (Java 15). With animations, a JVM tracer, 9 practice problems, quiz and interview scenarios.

lessons.title: Before you start: computer basics, files, servers and how to use this course
lessons.description: The foundation for learning Linux: CPU, RAM and disk, files, folders and paths, clients and servers, GUI vs command line, why servers run Linux, and how to use this course. With animations, real-time scenarios, real Bash you can run in the browser, and interview questions.

lessons.title: What is an operating system? Kernel, shell and the story of Unix and Linux
lessons.description: What an operating system does, what the Linux kernel and the shell are, user space vs kernel space, system calls, monolithic vs microkernel, and the history from Unix (1969) and GNU (1983) to Linux (1991). With animations, real Bash and strace, and interview questions.

lessons.title: Linux distributions explained: Ubuntu, Debian, Fedora, RHEL, Rocky, Arch
lessons.description: What a Linux distribution is, the Debian, Red Hat, SUSE, Arch and Alpine families, apt vs dnf, LTS vs rolling releases, support lifecycles and the CentOS end of life, and how to identify any Linux system from /etc/os-release. With animations, real Bash and interview questions.

lessons.title: Linux vs Unix vs Windows vs macOS, open source and the GPL
lessons.description: How Linux, Unix, Windows and macOS really differ (kernels, tools, paths, case sensitivity, line endings), what open source, copyleft and the GPL mean, and the cross-platform traps that break scripts and websites. With animations, real Bash and interview questions.

lessons.title: Installing Linux: WSL on Windows, VirtualBox, dual boot and a cloud VM
lessons.description: Five ways to get Linux compared: browser runner, WSL 2 on Windows, a VirtualBox virtual machine, dual boot and a cloud VM. Step-by-step WSL installation, how WSL really works, sharing files with Windows, the invisible password, cloud VM safety, and post-install checks with real Bash.

lessons.title: Terminal, console, shell and prompt: your first commands
lessons.description: The difference between terminal, console, shell and prompt; the structure of a command (command, options, arguments); reading the prompt; your first fifteen Linux commands; getting help with man and --help; Tab completion, history, Ctrl+C and other shortcuts. With animations and real Bash.

modules.title: The Linux file system
modules.summary: Everything is a file: the directory tree, moving around, paths, file types and getting help.

lessons.title: Everything is a file: the Linux directory hierarchy
lessons.description: The Linux directory tree explained: one root /, the Filesystem Hierarchy Standard (/etc, /home, /usr, /var, /tmp, /dev, /proc, /sys, /boot, /opt), merged /usr, real vs virtual file systems, mounts, and what “everything is a file” really means. Animations, a layer-by-layer dissection, real Bash and interview questions.

lessons.title: Moving around: pwd, cd and ls
lessons.description: pwd, cd and ls explained from zero: every form of cd (~, .., -, /), the ls options that matter (-l -a -h -t -r -S -d -R -F), reading ls -l column by column, why cd is a shell builtin, PWD and OLDPWD, and pwd vs pwd -P with symbolic links. Animations, real Bash and interview questions.

lessons.title: Absolute and relative paths, ~, . and .. and Tab completion
lessons.description: Absolute vs relative paths in Linux explained from zero: /, ~, ~user, . and .., Tab and double-Tab completion, realpath, dirname and basename, why ./script.sh is needed, how the kernel walks a path one folder at a time, and how to write scripts that work from any folder. Animations, real Bash and interview questions.

lessons.title: File types and hidden files: file, stat and ls -la
lessons.description: Linux file types explained: the seven types (- d l c b p s), why extensions do not matter, the file command and magic numbers, stat and the three timestamps atime, mtime and ctime (plus Birth), device major and minor numbers, named pipes, sockets, and hidden dotfiles with ls -a and ls -A. Animations, real Bash and interview questions.

lessons.title: Getting help: man, --help, info, whatis and apropos
lessons.description: How to find help on any Linux system without the internet: --help, man pages and their sections (1–8), moving and searching inside man, reading SYNOPSIS notation ([ ], ..., UPPERCASE), whatis, apropos and man -k, help for bash builtins, info manuals, mandb and where documentation is stored. Animations, real Bash and interview questions.

modules.title: Working with files and directories
modules.summary: Create, copy, move, sync, rename (one file or hundreds), delete and view files, use wildcards safely, and everyday utilities like date, bc and watch.

lessons.title: Creating files and folders: touch, mkdir and rmdir
lessons.description: Create folders with mkdir and mkdir -p (whole trees, idempotent scripts, -m permissions), empty files and timestamps with touch (-c, -a, -m, -d, -t, -r), remove empty folders with rmdir (-p), and create files with content using echo, printf, cat and here-documents. Every command explained, then used in development, DBA, data engineering, DevOps, security, testing and system administration, with real Bash outputs.

lessons.title: Copying, moving and syncing: cp, mv and rsync
lessons.description: Copy files and folders with cp (-r, -a, -p, -i, --update=none, -u, --backup), move and rename with mv (-i, -n, -v) and why mv is instant on the same disk, and keep backups up to date with rsync (-av, --delete, --dry-run, --exclude, trailing slash, -z over SSH). Every command explained, then used in DBA, DevOps, data, security, testing and development work, with real outputs.

lessons.title: Deleting safely: rm, rm -r, rm -i, shred and why rm -rf is dangerous
lessons.description: Delete files and folders with rm (-r, -d, -i, -I, -f, -v, --), the five dangers of rm (spaces, wildcards, empty variables, wrong machine, -f), guarded delete scripts with ${var:?}, why a deleted file can still use disk space (lsof +L1, truncate), and secure deletion with shred and its limits on SSDs. Explained, then used by admins, DBAs, data engineers, DevOps, QA and security teams, with real outputs.

lessons.title: Wildcards and globbing: *, ?, [ ] and brace expansion
lessons.description: Select files by pattern with *, ? and [ ] (ranges, [!…], [[:digit:]]), generate names with brace expansion ({a,b}, {01..12}, steps), and handle no-match, hidden files, quotes and spaces. Advanced: bash expansion order, nullglob, failglob, dotglob, nocaseglob, globstar ** and extglob !(…). Each pattern explained, then used by data engineers, admins, developers, QA, security and DevOps, with real outputs.

lessons.title: Viewing files: cat, tac, less, more, head, tail -f, nl and wc
lessons.description: Read files without an editor: cat and tac (-n, -b, -s, -A, joining files), head and tail (-n, -n +N, -c, line ranges, skipping CSV headers), tail -f, -F and --pid for live logs and log rotation, less and more (search, G, F, -S, -N), nl (-ba, -bp, -nrz, -w, -s) and wc (-l, -w, -c, -m). Each command explained, then used by admins, data engineers, developers, DBAs, QA, security and ML teams, with real outputs.

lessons.title: Everyday utilities: date, cal, bc, seq, sleep, time and watch
lessons.description: date formats (%F %T %Y %m %d %H %M %S %A %B %s), date arithmetic with -d (+45 days, yesterday, @timestamps), time zones with TZ and -u, setting the clock; cal and ncal; bc with scale, powers, -l, number bases and decimal comparisons; seq with steps, -w, -s and -f; sleep, timeout, time (real/user/sys) and watch (-n, -d, -g). Each tool explained, then used by admins, DBAs, data engineers, developers, DevOps, QA and ML teams, with real outputs.

lessons.title: Bulk renaming with rename and regular expressions
lessons.description: Rename many files at once with Perl rename: s/// with g and i, y/// for case, -n preview, -v, -f; regex building blocks for file names (^ $ . * + ? {n,m}, [ ], \d \w \s \b and their opposites, groups and $1, a|b); quoting traps such as $(date) in single quotes; Perl rename vs util-linux rename on RHEL; portable alternatives with bash loops and mv. Verified results, used by data, web, ML, security and operations teams.

lessons.title: nano: the beginner-friendly editor
lessons.description: Edit files in the terminal with GNU nano: open, save (Ctrl+O, Ctrl+S) and exit (Ctrl+X), cut, copy and paste lines (Ctrl+K, Ctrl+U, Alt+A, Alt+6), search, replace and go to line (Ctrl+W, Ctrl+\, Ctrl+_), undo (Alt+U), line numbers, backups (-B), read-only view (-v), sudoedit for system files, ~/.nanorc and the EDITOR variable. Real recorded nano screens and examples for admins, developers, DBAs, data and DevOps teams.

lessons.title: vim basics: modes, moving, editing and saving
lessons.description: vi and vim from zero: Normal, Insert, Command-line and Visual modes; i a o I A O and Esc; moving with h j k l (j down, k up), w b e, 0 $, gg G and :N; x, dd, yy, p, P, r, cw, counts, u and Ctrl+R; :w :q :wq :q! ZZ; searching with / ? n N; swap files and vimtutor. Every key verified by really typing it into vim, real screens, and examples for admins, developers, DBAs and data teams.

lessons.title: vim power use: search and replace, blocks, registers and .vimrc
lessons.description: vim beyond the basics: :s and :%s with ranges and the g, c and i flags, groups and \v; :g and :v on matching lines; visual, line and block mode (Ctrl+V insert and append, indent, case); the dot command, macros (qa … q, @a), registers and text objects (ciw, ci", dap); :sort, :r !cmd and :%!filter; splits, buffers and vimdiff; and a practical ~/.vimrc. Every result verified by typing the keys into a real vim, with real vimdiff screens.

lessons.title: Redirection: >, >>, <, 2>, 2>&1, /dev/null and here-documents
lessons.description: Every redirection operator: > and >> (overwrite and append), noclobber and >|, < for input, 2> and 2>>, 2>&1, &> and &>>, why the order of 2>&1 matters, /dev/null, here-documents (<< EOF, quoted EOF, <<-), here-strings (<<<), process substitution, and sudo tee. lessons.title: Pipes and tee: building command pipelines
lessons.description: The pipe | and how to build pipelines from small filters (head, tail, wc, grep, sort, uniq, cut, tr, awk) step by step; tee, tee -a and sudo tee; PIPESTATUS, set -o pipefail and SIGPIPE (141); |& and 2>&1 |; the subshell trap; named pipes with mkfifo. Explained, then used by admins, web, security, data, developers, DBAs, DevOps and QA, with real outputs and corrected classroom examples.

lessons.title: Chaining commands: ;, &&, ||, exit codes, $( ) and xargs
