modules.title: Start here: why Spark?
modules.summary: Prerequisites, the Spark story, architecture, the life of a job and your own Spark 4 lab.

lessons.title: Prerequisites: Python, SQL and Hadoop in one lesson
lessons.description: Everything you need before PySpark, checked on a real laptop with PySpark 4.3.0, Python 3.13 and Java 21: what happens without Java (JAVA_GATEWAY_EXITED), the filter/map/reduce/group patterns in plain Python, the same city report in pandas and PySpark, one bad row turning a column into a string, Spark 4’s ANSI cast errors and try_cast, how a file becomes partitions, and when pandas stops being enough.

lessons.title: What is Apache Spark? From MapReduce to Spark 4
lessons.description: What Apache Spark is, where it came from and why it replaced MapReduce for most work, shown with real PySpark 4.3.0 outputs: Spark SQL, the DataFrame API, the pandas API on Spark, MLlib and Structured Streaming on the same 5,000,000 orders; three questions taking 6.6 s without cache and 1.6 s with it; Spark 4 SQL pipe syntax and VARIANT; Spark’s components, history from 2009 to 4.3.0, and when not to use Spark.

lessons.title: Spark architecture: driver, executors and cluster managers
lessons.description: How a Spark application is organised, shown on a real Spark 4.3.0 standalone cluster: local mode as one JVM, a master granting executors with 2 cores and 1 GiB, the driver scheduling every task while running none itself, client versus cluster deploy mode (refused for Python on standalone), and a worker stopped in the middle of a job: lost executor, FetchFailed after 77 seconds, resubmitted tasks and a correct result. Plus standalone, YARN and Kubernetes compared.

lessons.title: How a PySpark program becomes jobs, stages and tasks
lessons.description: Follow one PySpark program through Spark 4.3.0 with real outputs and Spark UI screenshots: three transformations in 334 ms with no jobs, a typo caught before any job, two actions becoming five jobs with AQE and skipped stages, the Exchange that splits stages, four tasks reading 1,250,000 rows each and shuffling only 32 rows thanks to partial aggregation, and the Jobs, Stages and SQL tabs that show it all.

lessons.title: Install PySpark 4.3 and a Docker Spark cluster
lessons.description: Set up the course lab with real outputs: pip install pyspark 4.3.0 (280 JARs, 486 MB), spark-submit and the pyspark shell, a first program in local mode, one Docker image with Python 3.12 and Java 21 for every role, a Compose file for a standalone master, two workers and a history server, the first cluster job, the 5,000,000-order dataset, and a deliberate Python 3.13 vs 3.12 mismatch that breaks a lambda.

lessons.title: SparkContext, SparkConf and SparkFiles
lessons.description: How PySpark connects to a cluster: SparkConf settings and precedence, the SparkContext inside every SparkSession, the one-context-per-process rule, shipping files with addFile and SparkFiles.get, shipping Python modules with addPyFile, and executor environment variables. Real Spark 4.3 cluster outputs.

modules.title: RDD foundations
modules.summary: Spark's core abstraction: partitions, lineage, lazy evaluation and shuffles.

lessons.title: What is an RDD? Partitions, immutability and lineage
lessons.description: Resilient Distributed Datasets explained with real PySpark 4.3.0 outputs: creating RDDs with parallelize, textFile, wholeTextFiles and df.rdd; seeing partitions with glom(); immutability and lineage with toDebugString(); the five properties of an RDD; and the same city-revenue question taking 4.0 s as a DataFrame and 30.2 s as an RDD.

lessons.title: RDD transformations and actions
lessons.description: The RDD operations you will use most, with real PySpark 4.3.0 outputs on TiffinGo order notes: map vs flatMap (5,000 lines → 12,671 dishes), filter, distinct, union, sample, mapPartitions (4 setups instead of 100,000), collect, take, top, takeOrdered, reduce, fold, aggregate, countByValue and saveAsTextFile, plus the closure trap (a driver counter that stays 0, an accumulator that works) and where print() goes on a cluster.

lessons.title: Lazy evaluation, lineage and the DAG
lessons.description: How Spark’s laziness really behaves, measured with PySpark 4.3.0: a division by zero accepted at definition and raised at count(), the lineage of a word count read line by line with toDebugString(), a tokenizer running 48,000 times without cache and 24,000 with it, take(5) running 1 task while count() runs 3, and on the cluster a second action skipping its map stage because Spark reused the shuffle files (14.0 s → 0.2 s), with real DAG screenshots.

lessons.title: Narrow vs wide transformations and the shuffle
lessons.description: Narrow and wide dependencies measured on a Spark 4.3.0 cluster with 2,000,000 TiffinGo order amounts: map and filter with 0 bytes of shuffle, groupByKey writing 355.6 KiB in 5.0 s against reduceByKey’s 106.7 KiB in 2.3 s with identical results, repartition(2) shuffling 11.5 MiB while coalesce(2) shuffles nothing, a join that shuffles both sides, a co-partitioned join with no new shuffle, and mapValues keeping the partitioner while map loses it.

lessons.title: Pair RDDs and the word count
lessons.description: The classic PySpark word count on 24,000 real-looking TiffinGo reviews, the same result with DataFrames (split, explode, groupBy), and the pair-RDD toolkit on orders: countByKey, aggregateByKey for averages per city, combineByKey for (min, max), sortByKey, and a join of 50,001 orders with 2,000 customers for revenue per plan, with checks that catch join mistakes. Real PySpark 4.3.0 outputs throughout.

modules.title: Persistence and shared variables
modules.summary: Keep data in memory, share values with executors, and recover from failures.

lessons.title: cache and persist: storage levels
lessons.description: Caching in Spark 4.3.0, measured: cache() is lazy, DataFrames default to MEMORY_AND_DISK in a compressed columnar format (4.75 M orders in 47.5 MiB), PySpark RDDs to serialised MEMORY_ONLY; MEMORY_ONLY, MEMORY_AND_DISK and DISK_ONLY compared on a cluster (second query 6.7 s uncached vs 2.1–2.7 s cached, 651 MiB), the Storage tab, CACHE TABLE vs CACHE LAZY TABLE, and how caching four huge partitions killed every executor with exit code 52.

lessons.title: Broadcast variables and accumulators
lessons.description: Spark’s shared variables, measured on a Spark 4.3.0 cluster: a 400,000-entry lookup dictionary in a closure (14.8 s for 3 jobs, 2.1 MiB shipped per job) vs a broadcast variable (8.2 s, sent once), what unpersist() and destroy() really do in PySpark, a broadcast hash join (4.8 s) vs a sort-merge join (6.1 s), accumulators that double count inside transformations but are exact in actions and across task retries, and a custom dictionary accumulator for data quality.

lessons.title: Checkpointing and fault tolerance
lessons.description: How Spark survives failures and when to checkpoint, measured with PySpark 4.3.0: a lineage growing to 92 lines through unions and cut to 2 by a checkpoint, the extra job that computes an uncached RDD twice (20,000 vs 10,000 calls), localCheckpoint, a 400-step DataFrame loop going from 9.9 s to 5.7 s with periodic checkpoints, and a worker stopped on the cluster: a cached RDD recomputed 200,000 expensive calls while a checkpointed one recomputed none.

lessons.title: Serialization in PySpark
lessons.description: How PySpark turns code and data into bytes: cloudpickle for functions and closures, pickle and marshal serializers for RDD records, AutoBatchedSerializer, Apache Arrow for pandas conversions and vectorized UDFs, Kryo on the JVM side, closure size, broadcast and unpicklable objects. Real PySpark 4.3 measurements.

modules.title: DataFrame basics
modules.summary: The API used in industry: SparkSession, schemas and column operations.

lessons.title: SparkSession and DataFrames
lessons.description: The SparkSession entry point and the DataFrame, tested with PySpark 4.3.0: a second getOrCreate() that silently changed shuffle partitions from 8 to 50, newSession() with its own views and SQL conf, a first DataFrame from TiffinGo orders where one "abc" made amount a string, a query that ran 0 jobs until show() ran 2, the physical plan with a pushed filter, Row objects, and a DataFrame and SQL query with identical plans.

lessons.title: Creating DataFrames and schemas
lessons.description: Every way to create a PySpark DataFrame and how to declare its schema, tested with PySpark 4.3.0: tuples, Rows, dicts (columns come out sorted), pandas, RDDs and range; inference that fails on [1, 2.5] but silently turns [1, "two"] into strings; DDL strings and StructType with DECIMAL and nullable checks; nested array, struct and map columns; schemas saved as JSON; and inferSchema on 2M CSV rows costing 2 jobs and 4.6 s versus 0 jobs with a declared schema.

lessons.title: Working with columns
lessons.description: Selecting, adding, renaming, casting and filtering columns in PySpark 4.3.0 on TiffinGo orders: four ways to name a column, select and selectExpr, an ANSI cast that fails on one "abc" while try_cast returns null, withColumn and withColumns, when/otherwise and the null that falls into otherwise, filter traps (missing brackets, Python and) and a typo caught at analysis, plus 300 columns added in 6.87 s with a withColumn loop versus 0.98 s with withColumns.

lessons.title: Nulls and duplicates
lessons.description: Handling missing values and duplicate rows in PySpark 4.3.0 on a dirty TiffinGo sign-up export: null counts per column, "NA" strings and NaN that are not null, three-valued logic that made 404 + 1,642 miss 154 rows, count(col) and avg skipping nulls, na.drop keeping only 742 of 2,200 rows, type-aware na.fill, distinct versus dropDuplicates, and proof that dropDuplicates keeps different rows on different runs while row_number() does not.

lessons.title: Sorting, distinct, limit and union
lessons.description: orderBy, sortWithinPartitions, limit, distinct and union in PySpark 4.3.0 on 5 million orders: a global sort that shuffled 120 MiB in 6.7 s against 2.0 s with no shuffle within partitions, where nulls go, a top-5 query planned as TakeOrderedAndProject in 0.8 s, exact versus approximate distinct counts (3,999 vs 3,985), union matching columns by position so that "Card" became a city, unionByName with allowMissingColumns, and intersect, subtract and exceptAll.

lessons.title: collect, toPandas and Arrow
lessons.description: Bringing Spark data into Python with PySpark 4.3.0: first, take, tail, collect and toLocalIterator; one million rows timed with collect (8.4 s), toPandas without Arrow (9.9 s) and with Arrow (1.4 s), and the new toArrow (0.65 s); Arrow enabled by default since Spark 4.2; an INT column with a null turning into float64; pandas back to Spark 11.8 s vs 2.6 s; and spark.driver.maxResultSize stopping a 5-million-row collect before the driver ran out of memory.

modules.title: Reading and writing data
modules.summary: Files, formats, save modes and databases.

lessons.title: CSV and JSON
lessons.description: Reading messy CSV and JSON with PySpark 4.3.0: a real partner file where default options produced 8 rows from 7 orders, header, schema, multiLine and escape for quoted line breaks and doubled quotes, _corrupt_record in PERMISSIVE mode, DROPMALFORMED giving 6 rows for count() but 4 for all columns, FAILFAST, dateFormat, JSON Lines versus JSON arrays, nested structs and explode, a gzip CSV read by one task (3.4 s vs 2.0 s), and JSON inference.

lessons.title: Parquet, ORC and Avro
lessons.description: 5 million orders written as CSV, JSON, Parquet, ORC and Avro with PySpark 4.3.0: sizes from 557 MiB (JSON) to 36 MiB (ORC), a Pune revenue query from 2.74 s to 0.37 s, column pruning (0.46 s vs 0.17 s), row-group skipping that read 80,000 instead of 3.88 million rows on sorted data, the schema stored in the file, mergeSchema for a new column, a type change that cannot be merged, and snappy vs zstd vs gzip compression.

lessons.title: Writing data and small files
lessons.description: Writing DataFrames with PySpark 4.3.0: part files and _SUCCESS, save modes, partitionBy with partition pruning (498,646 of 5,000,000 rows read), the small-files problem where a groupBy written with partitionBy made 421 files of 1 KiB until repartition("city") made 8 (read back 1.33 s vs 0.28 s), maxRecordsPerFile, static partition overwrite deleting other cities versus dynamic overwrite, and saveAsTable.

lessons.title: JDBC, XML and other sources
lessons.description: Spark and PostgreSQL 16 over JDBC with PySpark 4.3.0: a connection refused for the JVM time zone Asia/Calcutta, writing 1M orders with batchsize, a plain read in one partition, a parallel read whose generated WHERE clauses we logged, skew from bounds ([0, 375000, 625000, 0]) and bounds that do not filter (all 1M rows in the last partition), filter pushdown visible in the database log, the query option, plus the built-in XML source of Spark 4, text and binaryFile.

modules.title: Transformations in depth
modules.summary: Aggregations, joins, window functions, built-in functions and UDFs.

lessons.title: groupBy and pivot
lessons.description: Aggregations in PySpark 4.3.0 on 5 million orders: several aggregates in one groupBy, partial aggregation visible in the plan, null keys as a group, rollup and cube subtotals (7 vs 9 rows), pivot without values running 4 extra jobs (2.72 s vs 1.30 s) and dropping an empty REFUNDED column, the 10,000-value pivot limit, unpivot back to 24 rows, and collect_list / collect_set.

lessons.title: Joins
lessons.description: Joins in PySpark 4.3.0: inner, left, right, full, left_semi, left_anti and cross on a small example; null keys that never match and eqNullSafe; AMBIGUOUS_REFERENCE after joining on an expression; a duplicate lookup key that turned 498,646 Pune orders into 997,292 rows; an inner join with an incomplete customer table that kept 2,498,734 of 5,000,000 orders; and broadcast (0.8 s) versus sort-merge (3.2 s) joins.

lessons.title: Window functions
lessons.description: Window functions in PySpark 4.3.0: row_number, rank and dense_rank on ties, lag and lead for day-over-day change, the default RANGE frame that repeated a running total (1210 twice) versus rowsBetween, moving averages and share of total, top-2 orders per city on 5M rows planned with WindowGroupLimit, and a window without partitionBy that collapsed 4 partitions into 1 (12.0 s vs 7.1 s).

lessons.title: String and date functions
lessons.description: Built-in string and datetime functions in PySpark 4.3.0: trimming, case, regexp_replace for phone numbers, regexp_extract, split_part and concat_ws; parsing dates in several formats with try_to_date and coalesce while to_date fails under ANSI; date arithmetic and date_trunc; the YYYY week-based-year pattern rejected by Spark with ISO week 53 spanning two years; and the session time zone changing how the same instant is displayed.

lessons.title: Complex data and VARIANT
lessons.description: Arrays, maps, structs and the Spark 4 VARIANT type in PySpark 4.3.0: transform, filter, aggregate and arrays_zip inside arrays, explode (5 rows) vs explode_outer (6), map and struct access, from_json turning a whole record null on one bad field, schema_of_json missing a field, parse_json and variant_get extracting fields independently, INVALID_VARIANT_CAST vs try_variant_get, and one field read from 1M payloads in about 2 s as text vs 0.62 s as stored VARIANT.

lessons.title: UDFs
lessons.description: User-defined functions in PySpark 4.3.0 on 5M orders: the same label as a built-in expression (0.85 s), a pickled Python UDF (3.50 s), an Arrow-optimised UDF (2.31 s, default since Spark 4.2) and a pandas UDF (2.10 s); BatchEvalPython in the plan; a UDF filter that disabled Parquet pushdown (4.09 s); a crash on None; a UDF declared int returning 472.5 giving None or 472 silently; and Spark 4 SQL UDFs with no Python step.

modules.title: Spark SQL
modules.summary: SQL, the catalog, the Hive metastore and the optimiser.

lessons.title: Spark SQL and views
lessons.description: Spark SQL and views in PySpark 4.3.0: spark.sql returning DataFrames, temp views invisible to a new session while a global temp view returned 5,000,000 rows, a view that still counted 3 rows after 5 were appended until REFRESH TABLE, views on views, SQL injection through an f-string (5,000,000 rows) versus named parameters (0 rows), Spark 4 pipe syntax, and analysis errors.

lessons.title: Tables, catalog and Hive metastore
lessons.description: Tables and catalogs in PySpark 4.3.0 with an embedded Hive metastore: enableHiveSupport, managed tables with saveAsTable and external tables with LOCATION, partitions and ANALYZE TABLE statistics (200,000 rows, 8 distinct cities), the catalog API, tables reopened by name from a second application while the temp view was gone, DROP TABLE deleting managed files but keeping external ones, and MSCK REPAIR TABLE registering a hand-written partition.

lessons.title: Catalyst and explain
lessons.description: The Catalyst optimizer read through explain() in PySpark 4.3.0: parsed, analyzed, optimized and physical plans of a 5M-order join, filters pushed below the join and into Parquet (5 PushedFilters), constant folding of (1 + 1) + 798 into 800, column pruning, a broadcast join chosen by size, explain formatted and cost, whole-stage code generation with 2 generated stages, identical plans for "bad" and "good" code, and a UDF filter Catalyst could not push.

lessons.title: Adaptive Query Execution
lessons.description: Adaptive Query Execution measured with PySpark 4.3.0 on 5M orders: AQE off vs on for a groupBy (204 tasks, 1.74 s vs 5 tasks, 0.62 s) with AQEShuffleRead coalesced, a sort-merge join switched to a broadcast join at run time (0.89 s vs 0.05 s), and a join on a key holding 60% of rows (3.67 s off, 2.57 s with coalescing, 1.92 s with skew-join splitting and SortMergeJoin(skew=true)), plus the settings and thresholds that control it.

modules.title: Performance tuning
modules.summary: Make slow jobs fast, with measurements.

lessons.title: Partitions and shuffle partitions
lessons.description: Spark partitions measured with PySpark 4.3.0 on 5M orders: how maxPartitionBytes and cores decide input partitions, 2,000 small files vs 8 files (4.06 s vs 0.20 s), a groupBy with 1 to 2,000 shuffle partitions (best 1.82 s, worst 8.13 s, AQE coalesced 200 to 8 tasks), rows per partition for repartition, repartition by column and coalesce, and the coalesce(1) trap.

lessons.title: Join strategies
lessons.description: Spark join strategies measured with PySpark 4.3.0: 5M orders joined to 4,000 customers with broadcast, shuffle_hash, merge and shuffle_replicate_nl hints (1.55 s, 4.53 s, 6.73 s, CartesianProduct), Exchange counts in the plan, forcing a broadcast of a 5M-row side, and bucketed tables that sort-merge join with zero shuffles (1.68 s vs 5.31 s).

lessons.title: Data skew and salting
lessons.description: Data skew measured with PySpark 4.3.0 on 6M orders where one restaurant has 60%: task duration and shuffle records from the Spark REST API for a skewed window (one task read 3.9M rows), a groupBy saved by partial aggregation, a skewed join, a salted join with exploded salts, AQE skew-join splitting (max task 2.8 s to 1.3 s), and isolating the hot key (17.2 s to 10.8 s).

lessons.title: Memory, spill and OOM
lessons.description: Spark memory measured with PySpark 4.3.0: the unified memory model ((heap − 300 MB) × 0.6), the same sort of 5M wide rows at 3 GB (no spill) and 1 GB (736 MiB spilled, 91 MiB on disk), spill removed with 64 partitions, a real java.lang.OutOfMemoryError from collect_list per city, and three fixes that work at 1 GB, plus memoryOverhead and driver OOMs.

lessons.title: Resources and dynamic allocation
lessons.description: Executor resources measured on a real Spark 4.3.0 standalone cluster: static allocation holding 4 executors, a spark.cores.max cap, dynamic allocation with shuffle tracking scaling 0 → 4 → 0 → 4 executors (with the ramp-up cost: 45.0 s vs 30.9 s), an executor larger than any worker waiting forever, and how to size executor cores, memory and counts.

lessons.title: Spark UI troubleshooting
lessons.description: Troubleshooting with the Spark UI using real Spark 4.3.0 screenshots: the SQL / DataFrame tab with named jobs, the plan graph with per-operator time (Sort 8.0 s after an Exchange of 6,000,000 rows), a skewed stage (median 2 s, max 5 s, one task reading 4.2M records) and a spilling stage (even tasks, 184 MiB spill each), plus a symptom-to-cause table, the History Server and the REST API.

lessons.title: Profiling and tracking from code
lessons.description: Find slow Python inside Spark: the Spark 4 UDF profiler (perf and memory), reading cProfile output, the classic RDD profiler (spark.python.profile, BasicProfiler), and tracking running jobs and stages from code with StatusTracker and job groups. Real PySpark 4.3 lab: a UDF profiled and fixed from 29.5 s to 0.85 s.

modules.title: Structured Streaming
modules.summary: Real-time data with the DataFrame API.

lessons.title: Streaming concepts
lessons.description: Structured Streaming concepts with PySpark 4.3.0: streaming DataFrames from readStream, why count() fails, the unbounded-table model, micro-batches with a 2 second trigger (100 rows per batch in about 0.4 s) read from lastProgress, triggers (default, processingTime, availableNow, continuous), and an availableNow file stream that restarts from its checkpoint and reads only the new file.

lessons.title: Sources and sinks
lessons.description: Structured Streaming sources and sinks with PySpark 4.3.0 and a real Kafka 3.9 broker: the fixed Kafka schema (binary key and value), parsing JSON with from_json, maxOffsetsPerTrigger splitting 600 events into batches of 248, 248 and 104, a Parquet file sink, foreachBatch writing city totals to PostgreSQL, a Kafka sink, the console sink, and why startingOffsets is ignored on an existing checkpoint.

lessons.title: Output modes, event time and watermarks
lessons.description: Event-time windows and watermarks with PySpark 4.3.0, batch by batch: five deterministic micro-batches with late orders into 5-minute windows, complete vs update vs append output modes, the error for append without a watermark, a 5-minute watermark finalising each window once (watermark 10:06, 10:11, 10:17), a very late order dropped (numRowsDroppedByWatermark = 1) instead of changing 1419 to 9196, and state bounded to 2 rows.

lessons.title: Windowed aggregations and stream joins
lessons.description: Windows and joins in Structured Streaming with PySpark 4.3.0: the same five clicks in tumbling (3/1/1), sliding (3/4/2/1) and session windows (4 sessions), a stream-static join with inner and left joins, a stream-stream join of orders and deliveries within 30 minutes with watermarks where the left outer join emits undelivered orders after the watermark, and state growing 4 → 7 → 9 without watermarks.

lessons.title: Checkpoints, exactly-once and state
lessons.description: Fault tolerance in Structured Streaming with PySpark 4.3.0 and Kafka 3.9: restarting a Kafka query from its checkpoint (only the 500 new rows read), the offsets and commits logs, a simulated crash inside foreachBatch where a plain append wrote 2,099 rows for 1,500 orders and an idempotent batch_id write kept 1,500, deduplicating 1,800 events to 1,500 with dropDuplicatesWithinWatermark on the RocksDB state store, and STATE_STORE_KEY_SCHEMA_NOT_COMPATIBLE after changing a grouping key.

modules.title: Machine learning with MLlib
modules.summary: Pipelines, features and models at scale.

lessons.title: ML Pipelines
lessons.description: Spark MLlib pipelines with PySpark 4.3.0 on 200,000 customers: Transformers vs Estimators, StringIndexer learning Free/Silver/Gold, VectorAssembler, a five-stage churn Pipeline (Imputer, StringIndexer, OneHotEncoder, VectorAssembler, LogisticRegression) fitted in 6.2 s with test AUC 0.81, the rawPrediction/probability/prediction columns, an unseen city with handleInvalid keep vs error, and the null error without an Imputer.

lessons.title: Feature engineering and classification
lessons.description: Feature engineering and classifiers in Spark MLlib with PySpark 4.3.0: a median Imputer (4,797 nulls filled), StandardScaler z-scores, Bucketizer tenure bands (47.7% churn in the first 6 months), and logistic regression, decision tree, random forest and gradient-boosted trees on the same features (AUC 0.8105, 0.7447, 0.7867, 0.8069; fit 4.9 to 22.3 s), with coefficients, feature importances and the effect of scaling on regularized models.

lessons.title: Evaluation, tuning and saving models
lessons.description: Evaluating, tuning and saving Spark ML models with PySpark 4.3.0: ROC AUC 0.8105 and PR AUC 0.7174, accuracy 0.75 vs a 0.63 baseline, a confusion matrix, precision and recall at thresholds 0.3/0.5/0.7, TrainValidationSplit (17.3 s) vs CrossValidator (36.9 s) on a 6-point grid, and saving a 12.9 KB PipelineModel that reloads with identical predictions and scores 200,000 customers in 0.7 s.

lessons.title: Clustering and recommendations
lessons.description: Unsupervised learning and recommendations in PySpark MLlib: KMeans with scaling and silhouette to choose k, ALS collaborative filtering with rank, regParam and cold-start strategy, implicit feedback, and FPGrowth frequent itemsets with confidence and lift. Real PySpark 4.3 lab on TiffinGo data.

modules.title: Spark in production
modules.summary: Submitting, deploying, testing and the lakehouse.

lessons.title: spark-submit and deploy modes
lessons.description: spark-submit on a real Spark 4.3.0 standalone cluster: a PySpark job failing on executors with ModuleNotFoundError, fixed with --py-files, configuration precedence measured (code 12 beats --conf 100 beats properties file 50; --conf 1500m beats file 1g), client vs cluster deploy mode, and the error for Python cluster mode on standalone, plus options for shipping Python environments.

lessons.title: Spark on YARN and Kubernetes
lessons.description: Spark on YARN with a real Hadoop 3.4.1 cluster and Spark 4.3.0: client vs cluster mode, the five files uploaded to HDFS staging, the driver running in ApplicationMaster container 000001 with output only in yarn logs, and a job stuck in ACCEPTED because the only NodeManager was UNHEALTHY (disk over 90%), plus Spark-on-Kubernetes settings (images, service accounts, pod templates, shuffle tracking) from the official documentation.

lessons.title: Spark Connect
lessons.description: Spark Connect with Spark 4.3.0: a Connect server on sc://localhost:15002 and a thin Python client that starts no JVM (classic PySpark starts one), unchanged DataFrame code aggregating 5M orders on the server, sparkContext and df.rdd unsupported (JVM_ATTRIBUTE_NOT_SUPPORTED, NOT_IMPLEMENTED), analysis errors raised only when the server analyses the plan, isolated sessions, and Python UDFs running server-side.

lessons.title: Testing PySpark code
lessons.description: Unit-testing PySpark with pytest and pyspark.testing (PySpark 4.3.0): a pure delivery-fee transformation, a session-scoped SparkSession fixture started once in 5.3 s, assertDataFrameEqual (row order ignored) and assertSchemaEqual, a deliberately failing test whose DIFFERENT_ROWS diff marks the wrong Mumbai fee (60 vs 40), a 13.6 s suite, and the test pyramid from unit to data-quality checks.

lessons.title: Delta Lake and Iceberg
lessons.description: Delta Lake and Apache Iceberg with PySpark 4.1.1, delta-spark 4.3.1 and Iceberg 1.12.0: the _delta_log transaction log, UPDATE, DELETE and MERGE as versions 0–3, history and versionAsOf time travel, schema enforcement rejecting a string amount and mergeSchema adding a column, and Iceberg hidden partitioning with days(ts), snapshots, VERSION AS OF, column rename and partition evolution without rewriting data.

lessons.title: Writing clean, modular PySpark
lessons.description: How to structure PySpark code for production: small DataFrame-to-DataFrame functions, DataFrame.transform chains, configuration passed in, I/O at the edges and tests per function, plus plan-aware habits: select or withColumns instead of looped withColumn, toDF for renames, early filters and isEmpty instead of count. Real PySpark 4.3 measurements and pytest results.

modules.title: Spark in industry today
modules.summary: Platforms, alternatives and what is new in Spark 4.

lessons.title: Spark platforms
lessons.description: Spark platforms compared (November 2026): Databricks (Runtime 19 with Spark 4.2.0, 18 LTS with 4.1.0), Microsoft Fabric Runtime 2.0 (Spark 4.1), Amazon EMR (Spark 4.0.2), Google Serverless for Apache Spark runtime 3.0 (Spark 4.0.1), AWS Glue 5.1 (Spark 3.5.6) and open-source Spark 4.3.0, plus one unchanged PySpark job run on local mode, a standalone cluster and YARN (start-up 7.5 s, 10.7 s, 25.7 s) and how to choose a platform.

lessons.title: Spark vs pandas, Polars, DuckDB, Flink and Trino
lessons.description: A real benchmark of pandas 3.0, Polars 2.1, DuckDB 2.0 and PySpark 4.3 on 5M and 50M orders (2 CPUs, 8 GB): groupBy, join and top-3 per city timings and peak memory (DuckDB 0.03 s and 140 MB on 5M rows; pandas killed out of memory on 50M; Spark’s ~6 s start-up), and when to use Spark, single-node engines, Flink for low-latency streaming or Trino for federated interactive SQL.

lessons.title: What’s new in Spark 4
lessons.description: A hands-on tour of Spark 4.0 to 4.3 on PySpark 4.3.0: ANSI SQL mode by default (DIVIDE_BY_ZERO, CAST_INVALID_INPUT) and try_cast/try_divide, pipe syntax, session variables, UTF8_LCASE collation, SQL scripting with WHILE loops and recursive CTEs (4.1), Python UDTFs and the Python Data Source API, GEOMETRY types (4.2), and Spark 4.3’s UNNEST, jaro_winkler_similarity and flag-gated ASOF JOIN, plus an upgrade checklist from Spark 3.5.

lessons.title: Graph processing with GraphFrames
lessons.description: Graph analytics from PySpark with GraphFrames: vertices and edges as DataFrames, degrees, PageRank, connected components, shortest paths, label propagation and motif finding, GraphX vs GraphFrames, and setup for Spark 4. Real PySpark 4.3 lab with GraphFrames 0.12.3 on a referral network.

lessons.description: Capstone part 1: TiffinGo asks for a daily revenue and churn-feature pipeline. Plan a medallion (landing, silver, gold, quarantine) design, then profile 842,587 raw orders, 20,100 customers and 800 restaurants with PySpark: duplicates, bad and negative amounts, orphan keys, invalid phones and a 30% skewed restaurant, and turn every finding into a cleaning rule.

lessons.title: Build the pipeline
lessons.description: Capstone part 2: build the TiffinGo pipeline the production way. Pure, unit-tested PySpark transforms (clean_orders with try_cast and a quarantine reason, latest-row customers, broadcast-join daily city revenue, churn features), a pipeline script writing partitioned silver Parquet, quality gates that fail the run, JSON run metrics, and the same job submitted to a standalone cluster with --py-files.

courses.title: Apache Kafka
courses.tagline: Real-time event streaming used by Uber, Swiggy and every big app.

modules.title: Start here: why Kafka?
modules.summary: The event-streaming story, messaging models, architecture, topics and your own Kafka 4 lab.

lessons.title: What is Kafka?
lessons.description: What Apache Kafka is and why companies use it, shown on a real Kafka 4.4 cluster: one stream of TiffinGo order events read by kitchen, billing and analytics consumer groups independently, events that stay after reading, replay from history, and a real record batch dissected (offset, key, value, timestamp, producer id).

lessons.title: Messaging models: queue vs pub-sub
lessons.description: Point-to-point queues vs publish-subscribe, and how Kafka does both with consumer groups. Real Kafka 4.4 lab: three riders in one group share 12 orders (4 + 2 + 6), two groups each receive all 12, and a fourth consumer sits idle with no partition; plus where Kafka 4.x share groups fit.

lessons.title: Kafka architecture
lessons.description: Brokers, clusters, partition leaders and followers, ISR and the KRaft controller quorum, inspected on a real 3-node Kafka 4.4 cluster: quorum status, leaders per partition, internal topics, a broker data directory dissected, then a broker stopped and restarted to watch failover and preferred-leader recovery.

lessons.title: Topics, partitions and offsets
lessons.description: How Kafka splits a topic into partitions, numbers records with offsets and picks a partition from the key. Real Kafka 4.4 lab: keyed city orders (one partition left empty), murmur2 computed by hand to match the broker, seeking to an offset, adding partitions moves Mumbai from partition 1 to 4, and partitions can never be reduced.

lessons.title: Install Kafka 4 (KRaft) and the CLI tools
lessons.description: Run Apache Kafka 4.4 with one docker run command (KRaft, no ZooKeeper), read its default server.properties, and use the everyday CLI tools: kafka-topics (create, list, describe, delete), kafka-configs (live retention change), console producer and consumer. Includes the bin tool families dissected and three real error messages.

lessons.title: Two real-time projects: on a VM or in Colab
lessons.description: Build two real-time Kafka projects step by step on a Linux VM or in free Google Colab: a TiffinGo live order dashboard (revenue per city and big-order alerts) and a UPI fraud alert pipeline (payments → fraud detector with a 60-second sliding window → fraud-alerts topic → SMS notifier). Kafka 4.4 KRaft from the binary, Python confluent-kafka, a downloadable Colab notebook, and real outputs.

modules.title: Producers
modules.summary: How a record travels from your code to a partition leader, and how to make it fast and safe.

lessons.title: How a producer sends a message
lessons.description: Inside the Kafka producer: serializer, partitioner, record accumulator, sender thread and delivery callback. Real Kafka 4.4 lab with confluent-kafka: produce() returns in about 1 ms while confirmation arrives about 60 ms later, latency percentiles, a failed send that only the callback reports, plus the first producer settings, error types and timeouts.

lessons.title: Keys and partitioners
lessons.description: How Kafka producers choose partitions: explicit partition, key hashing (murmur2 in Java, consistent_random/CRC32 by default in librdkafka) and sticky partitioning for null keys, adaptive partitioning and custom partitioners. Real Kafka 4.4 lab: sticky batches seen in kafka-dump-log, the same key landing in different partitions with two partitioners, a hot key with 792 of 1,000 records, and a compound-key fix.

lessons.title: Batching and compression
lessons.description: How Kafka producers batch records (linger.ms, batch.size) and compress batches (gzip, snappy, lz4, zstd), where the broker stores or recompresses them, and the size limits. Real Kafka 4.4 lab with 20,000 JSON orders: 1,250 batches and 2.4 s with linger.ms=0 vs 20 batches and 0.06 s with 5 ms; on-disk size 2,268 KiB uncompressed vs 221 KiB gzip and 231 KiB zstd.

lessons.title: acks and durability
lessons.description: Kafka producer acks=0, 1 and all, the ISR, min.insync.replicas, NOT_ENOUGH_REPLICAS, high watermark, unclean leader election and eligible leader replicas. Real Kafka 4.4 lab: 58k vs 49k vs 37k records/s for acks 0/1/all, then a stopped broker makes acks=all refuse writes while acks=1 accepts and acks=0 returns no offset.

lessons.title: Idempotent producer and retries
lessons.description: How Kafka retries create duplicates and how the idempotent producer prevents them with a producer id, epoch and per-partition sequence numbers. Real Kafka 4.4 lab: a frozen follower delays acks=all, the producer retries, and one payment is stored three times with idempotence off but once with it on, proven with kafka-dump-log. Plus ordering with in-flight requests, retry backoff and what idempotence cannot cover.

modules.title: Consumers
modules.summary: Groups, rebalances, offsets, lag and delivery guarantees up to exactly-once.

lessons.title: Consumers and consumer groups
lessons.description: How Kafka consumers poll and fetch, and how consumer groups share partitions through a group coordinator with heartbeats and timeouts. Real Kafka 4.4 lab: one consumer reads 600 orders in 3 polls of 200, two more members join and the 6 partitions split 2-2-2, then kafka-consumer-groups shows members, coordinator k2 and state Stable. Plus key settings, max.poll.interval.ms and static membership.

lessons.title: Rebalancing and partition assignment
lessons.description: What triggers a Kafka consumer group rebalance and how partitions are reassigned: eager vs cooperative-sticky strategies in the classic protocol and the new server-side consumer protocol (KIP-848, production-ready in Kafka 4.0). Real Kafka 4.4 lab with live traffic: when a third consumer joins, eager takes away all 6 partitions, cooperative and KIP-848 only 2.

lessons.title: Offsets, commits and lag
lessons.description: Kafka consumer position vs committed offset, auto and manual (sync/async) commits, the __consumer_offsets topic, consumer lag and resetting offsets safely. Real Kafka 4.4 lab: a billing group commits after 120 orders, lag grows to 189 while it is down, a dry-run shift-by and a reset to earliest, and a real commit record printed from __consumer_offsets.

lessons.title: Delivery guarantees
lessons.description: At-most-once, at-least-once and exactly-once in Kafka, proven by crashing a consumer. Real Kafka 4.4 lab: 50 invoices, a hard crash after 25; committing before processing lost invoices 26 to 30, committing after processing sent 21 to 25 twice. Plus idempotent processing, idempotency keys, offsets stored with results, and what Kafka exactly-once covers.

lessons.title: Transactions and exactly-once
lessons.description: Kafka transactions: transactional.id, begin/commit/abort, the transaction coordinator, COMMIT and ABORT control markers, read_committed vs read_uncommitted, the last stable offset, send_offsets_to_transaction and zombie fencing. Real Kafka 4.4 lab: an aborted debit stays on disk but read_committed skips it, markers take offsets 3, 6 and 8, and a newer producer fences an older one.

modules.title: Storage internals
modules.summary: What is really on the broker disk: segments, indexes, retention, compaction and tiered storage.

lessons.title: The commit log and segments
lessons.description: How Kafka stores a partition on disk as a chain of segments: .log, .index, .timeindex, .snapshot, leader-epoch-checkpoint and partition.metadata, base-offset file names, the active segment and roll rules (segment.bytes, segment.ms). Real Kafka 4.4 lab: 10,000 orders roll into three 1 MiB segments, the 1 MiB minimum is enforced, and pre-allocated indexes shrink when a segment closes.

lessons.title: Indexes and how a read works
lessons.description: How a Kafka broker finds an offset: choose the segment by base-offset file name, binary-search the sparse memory-mapped offset index, scan a few batches; and how the time index turns timestamps into offsets. Real Kafka 4.4 lab: offset 5000 located by hand via segment 3413 and index entry 4999 → byte 488000, the 185-entry index dissected, and a consumer fetching offset 5000.

lessons.title: Retention and compaction
lessons.description: Kafka clean-up policies: time and size retention (retention.ms, retention.bytes), the log start offset, and log compaction with the log cleaner, tombstones, dirty ratio and delete.retention.ms. Real Kafka 4.4 lab: four segments deleted after 60 s retention with the log start jumping to 301, and a compacted menu-prices topic reduced from 11 records to the latest 3 with a deleted dish removed.

lessons.title: Tiered storage and zero-copy
lessons.description: Why Kafka is fast (sequential appends, OS page cache, batches end to end, zero-copy sendfile) and how tiered storage (KIP-405, production-ready in Kafka 3.9) moves closed segments to object storage with local.retention and remote.storage.enable. Real Kafka 4.4 lab: 300,000 × 1 KB records written at 46 MB/s and read back at about 63 MB/s from the page cache, with 1.9 GB cached outside the JVM.

modules.title: Replication and the cluster
modules.summary: Leaders, followers, ISR, failures and the KRaft controller quorum.

lessons.title: Brokers and replication
lessons.description: How Kafka replicates partitions across brokers: replication factor, leaders and followers, the preferred leader, round-robin and rack-aware replica placement, manual assignment and kafka-reassign-partitions with throttles. Real Kafka 4.4 lab: 6 partitions × RF 3 give 2 leaders and 6 replicas per broker, and a partition is moved from brokers 1,2 to 3,1 and disappears from broker 2’s disk.

lessons.title: ISR and the high watermark
lessons.description: The in-sync replica set (ISR), replica.lag.time.max.ms, the log end offset (LEO) and the high watermark (HW): why consumers only see committed records, and how acks and min.insync.replicas interact with a slow follower. Real Kafka 4.4 lab: a paused follower freezes the HW at 5, is removed from the ISR after about 10 s, and rejoins after it catches up.

lessons.title: Leader election
lessons.description: How Kafka elects partition leaders: failover from the ISR, leader epochs and fencing, preferred-leader elections and automatic rebalancing, controlled shutdown, unclean elections and Eligible Leader Replicas (KIP-966). Real Kafka 4.4 lab: a leader broker is killed during 160 writes and all 160 are delivered with a 9.8 s pause.

lessons.title: KRaft vs ZooKeeper
lessons.description: How Kafka stores cluster metadata: ZooKeeper mode versus KRaft (KIP-500), the controller quorum and Raft epochs, the __cluster_metadata log, broker observers, snapshots, feature levels, dynamic quorums and ZooKeeper-to-KRaft migration. Real Kafka 4.4 lab: quorum status, a dump of 24,618 metadata records and the metadata shell image.

modules.title: Queues and error handling
modules.summary: Share groups (queues for Kafka), retry topics and dead letter queues.

lessons.title: Share groups: queues for Kafka
lessons.description: Kafka share groups (KIP-932, Queues for Kafka): record-level distribution instead of partition assignment, acquisition locks, accept/release/reject acknowledgements, delivery count limits, the share-partition start offset and the share coordinator. Real Kafka 4.4 lab: 3,000 jobs shared without duplicates, rejected records archived, and released records redelivered exactly 5 times.

lessons.title: Retry topics and dead letter queues
lessons.description: Non-blocking error handling for Kafka consumers: poison messages and head-of-line blocking, transient versus permanent errors, retry-topic ladders with backoff, dead letter queues with diagnostic headers, ordering trade-offs, replay, and built-in DLQs in Kafka Connect and Spring Kafka. Real Kafka 4.4 lab with Python: 8 orders, 6 processed, 2 parked in the DLQ with full context.

modules.title: Kafka Connect
modules.summary: Moving data in and out of Kafka without writing code, including change data capture.

lessons.title: Kafka Connect: source and sink connectors
lessons.description: Kafka Connect explained: workers, connectors and tasks, source and sink connectors, converters and the JsonConverter schema envelope, single message transforms (SMTs), internal config/offset/status topics, the REST API, the offsets API, and error tolerance with a dead letter queue. Real Kafka 4.4 lab: a file streamed into Kafka with SMTs, live appends, a stored file position, and a bad JSON record routed to a DLQ with context headers.

lessons.title: Change data capture with Debezium
lessons.description: Log-based change data capture with Debezium on Kafka Connect: Postgres WAL and logical replication slots, snapshots, the change event envelope (before, after, source, op), tombstones, ExtractNewRecordState, slot lag, and the outbox pattern. Real lab: Postgres 16 and Debezium 3.7 on Kafka 4.4 turn INSERT, UPDATE and DELETE into events, and a change made while Connect was down still arrives.

modules.title: Schemas
modules.summary: Schema Registry, Avro and safe schema evolution.

lessons.title: Schema Registry and Avro
lessons.description: Why Kafka needs schemas, how a schema registry works (subjects, versions, global ids, the _schemas topic), the Confluent wire format byte by byte, Avro binary encoding, and Avro vs Protobuf vs JSON Schema. Real lab with Confluent Schema Registry 8.1 and Kafka 4.4: an order encoded in 20 bytes instead of 50, decoded by schema id, and a bad record rejected inside the producer.

lessons.title: Schema evolution and compatibility
lessons.description: How to change Kafka message schemas safely: writer and reader schemas, defaults, Avro schema resolution, BACKWARD, FORWARD, FULL, NONE and transitive compatibility modes, type promotion, renames with aliases, deploy order, and Protobuf/JSON Schema notes. Real lab: a 409 for a field without a default, and a 6-change × 4-mode compatibility matrix from Schema Registry 8.1.

modules.title: Stream processing
modules.summary: Kafka Streams, state, windows and joins, and Kafka with Spark.

lessons.title: Kafka Streams basics
lessons.description: Kafka Streams explained: a Java library for stream processing on Kafka, the KStream DSL, topologies and processors, stateless operations (filter, mapValues, split), serdes, tasks, stream threads, application.id and exactly-once. Real Kafka Streams 4.4 lab: a topology printed and run with 2 threads and 3 tasks, routing orders to two topics.

lessons.title: KTables and state stores
lessons.description: Stateful stream processing with Kafka Streams: stream–table duality, KTable and GlobalKTable, groupBy vs groupByKey, count/reduce/aggregate, RocksDB state stores, changelog and repartition topics, restore, standby replicas and interactive queries. Real Kafka Streams 4.4 lab: counts per item survive deleting all local state, restored from 9 changelog records.

lessons.title: Windows and joins
lessons.description: Time in Kafka Streams: event time and stream time, tumbling, hopping, sliding and session windows, grace periods and late records, suppress for final results, and stream–table and stream–stream joins. Real Kafka Streams 4.4 outputs (TopologyTestDriver): a late record counted within grace, one dropped after grace, sessions merging, orders enriched with live menu prices, and payments matched within 5 minutes.

lessons.title: Kafka with Spark and Flink
lessons.description: Processing Kafka with engines: Spark Structured Streaming (Kafka source schema, from_json, windows, watermarks, output modes, checkpoints and offsets) and Apache Flink (continuous processing, snapshots, Flink SQL), compared with Kafka Streams and ksqlDB. Real PySpark 4.3 lab on Kafka 4.4: 5-minute revenue per city, one late row dropped by the watermark, and offsets read from the checkpoint.

modules.title: Kafka in production
modules.summary: Monitoring, tuning, security and multi-cluster setups.

lessons.title: Monitoring and consumer lag
lessons.description: How to monitor Kafka in production: consumer lag (end minus committed offset) and lag in time, prefetching vs processing, broker JMX metrics (UnderReplicatedPartitions, OfflinePartitionsCount, ActiveControllerCount, idle percentages, request latencies), client statistics, disk usage and alert design. Real Kafka 4.4 lab with JMX: lag falling under a slow consumer, and URP jumping to 3 when a broker is paused.

lessons.title: Performance tuning and partition sizing
lessons.description: A measured approach to Kafka performance: producer batch.size, linger.ms, compression and acks; consumer fetch settings and parallelism; broker threads, disks and page cache; and partition sizing from measured per-partition throughput and consumer parallelism. Real Kafka 4.4 lab with perf-test tools: batching raised throughput from 16 to 64 MB/s, 12 partitions beat 1, and two popular tweaks did not help.

lessons.title: Security: TLS, SASL and ACLs
lessons.description: Securing Kafka: listeners and security protocols, TLS certificates, keystores and truststores, SASL authentication with SCRAM (and OAUTHBEARER, mTLS, Kerberos), principals, the KRaft StandardAuthorizer and ACLs for least privilege, super users and quotas. Real Kafka 4.4 lab: a SASL_SSL broker rejects plaintext, wrong passwords and untrusted certificates, and ACLs let billing write and kitchen read only.

lessons.title: Multi-cluster and MirrorMaker 2
lessons.description: Running more than one Kafka cluster: disaster recovery, aggregation, migration and geo-replication with MirrorMaker 2 (remote topics, heartbeats, checkpoints, offset syncs, group offset sync), active-passive vs active-active, RPO and RTO, and alternatives such as Cluster Linking. Real Kafka 4.4 lab: 1,000 orders mirrored to a DR cluster and a failover drill where the consumer resumed at a translated offset of 405 instead of 600.

modules.title: Kafka in industry
modules.summary: Managed platforms, alternatives and what is new in Kafka 4.

lessons.title: Managed Kafka platforms
lessons.description: Managed Kafka explained: what providers take over and what stays with you, serverless vs provisioned vs BYOC, Apache Kafka vs Kafka-compatible engines, and the landscape in late 2026 (Amazon MSK, Google Cloud Managed Service for Apache Kafka, Confluent Cloud, Azure Event Hubs, Aiven, Instaclustr, Redpanda, WarpStream). Includes a real sizing script: 19.5 MB/s in, 78 MB/s out, 6.8 TB and 24 partitions.

lessons.title: Kafka vs RabbitMQ, Pulsar and others
lessons.description: Kafka compared with RabbitMQ, Apache Pulsar, cloud queues (SQS, Pub/Sub, Service Bus), Kinesis, NATS and Redis Streams: queue vs log, retention and replay, routing, ordering, scaling and operations, with a decision guide. Real lab with RabbitMQ 4.4 and Kafka 4.4: acknowledged messages vanish from a queue, while a Kafka topic serves every group and replays.

lessons.title: What’s new in Kafka 4
lessons.description: Everything that changed in Apache Kafka 4.x: 4.0 removed ZooKeeper (KRaft only), made the KIP-848 consumer protocol GA and introduced queues; 4.1 previewed queues and the Streams rebalance protocol; 4.2 made share groups production-ready; 4.3 improved coordinators and Streams state; 4.4 added share-group dead letter queues and transactional state stores. Real lab: feature levels and group types of a Kafka 4.4 cluster.

modules.title: Capstone
modules.summary: Design, build and review a real-time TiffinGo order pipeline, then prepare for interviews.

lessons.title: Capstone: problem and design
lessons.description: Capstone part 1: turning TiffinGo’s order-processing requirements into a Kafka design: partitions and keys, replication and durability, exactly-once processing, dead letter queue, compacted reference data, Avro schemas, Connect sink and monitoring, with a decision table linking every choice to its lesson and three design reviews.

lessons.title: Capstone: build the pipeline
lessons.description: Capstone part 2: building the TiffinGo order pipeline end to end on Kafka 4.4: topics, an idempotent Avro producer with Schema Registry, an exactly-once Python processor with a compacted menu and a dead letter queue, a Kafka Connect sink with read_committed, and reconciliation. Real result: 1,841 enriched + 1,159 DLQ = 3,000 orders, lag 0, 1,841 lines in the sink.

lessons.title: Capstone: review and interview preparation
lessons.description: Capstone part 3: proving the pipeline under failure and preparing for interviews. A chaos test kills a broker during exactly-once processing and an independent audit finds all 6,000 orders exactly once; a review checklist covers data, durability, errors and operations; and an interview map links common Kafka questions to every lesson in the course.
